question: With the approval and publication of Regulation (EU) 2024/3236 amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1057 and (EU) 2021/1058 as regards Regional Emergency Support to Reconstruction (RESTORE), Member States may more easily channel the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) and the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) in their 2021-2027 operational programmes towards disaster reconstruction, such as the one in and around Valencia following the DANA (high-altitude isolated depression) in November 2024.

In this way, the ERDF and ESF+, both at national and regional level, will be able to pre-finance up to 25 % of the total amount of recovery projects and co-finance up to 95 % of their total cost. Given that this amendment entered into force on 20 December 2024: 1.

Has the European Commission received the Spanish Government’s request for the reprogramming of the 2021-2027 ERDF and ESF+ operational programmes, both at national and regional level, for the reconstruction work following the damage caused by the natural disaster in Spain, especially in Valencia?
If so, what amount has been redirected towards the new specific reconstruction objectives?
answer: The Commission has not received any request to divert the European Social Fund Plus and the European Regional Development Fund to sustain the reconstruction efforts following the damage caused by the natural disaster, especially in Valencia.

The Commission is informed that the Spanish authorities are working to determine the appropriate allocation, taking into consideration the ongoing mid-term review aimed at evaluating the progress of the 2021-2027 programmes.

The regional and national authorities can seize this opportunity to introduce the new specific objective RESTOR E (1) in the new version of the programmes, which are expected to be submitted to the Commission by 24 June 2025.

The RESTORE amendment proposals expected to be submitted by the Spanish authorities will detail the objectives and the financial allocations for reconstruction in the cohesion policy programmes. They will need to be approved by the Commission, in line with the funds’ regulations.

On 20 January 2025, the Spanish authorities submitted an application for financial assistance from the EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF) (2) and requested an advance payment. As the application is eligible for EUSF assistance, on 31 March 2025, the Commission disbursed an advance payment of EUR 100 million to Spain. This is the maximum amount allowed under the EUSF as advance payment.

As outlined in the regulation (EU) 2024/3236 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1057 and (EU) 2021/1058 as regards Regional Emergency Support to Reconstruction (RESTORE).
